title: Controlling Fraud in Small Business Health Benefits Programs in the United States, 1990-1996
description:
The focus of this project was insider fraud -- crimes
 committed by the owners and operators of insurance companies that were
 established for the purposes of defrauding businesses and
 employees. The quantitative data for this collection were taken from a
 database maintained by the National Association of Insurance
 Commissioners (NAIC), an organization that represents state insurance
 departments collectively and acts as a clearinghouse for information
 obtained from individual departments. Created in 1988, the Regulatory
 Information Retrieval System (RIRS) database contains information on
 actions taken by state insurance departments against individuals and
 firms, including cease and desist orders, license revocations, fines,
 and penalties imposed. Data available for this project include a total
 of 123 actions taken against firms labeled as Multiple Employer
 Welfare Arrangements or Multiple Employer Trusts (MEWA/MET) in the
 RIRS database. Variables available in this data collection include the
 date action was taken, state where action was taken, dollar amount of
the penalty imposed in the action, and disposition for action taken.
